provenance.notes_on_uncertainty: Claude pseudo-PCA target is loaded directly from the Claude branch export, not reconstructed from local Big Five profiles.

answers.does_claude_big_five_transfer_to_canonic: Yes. Big Five reaches R2 0.613 vs semantic baseline 0.389 (delta +0.224).
answers.does_codex_retained_transfer_to_claude_p: No under the direct Claude target. Codex retained features reach R2 0.166 vs baseline 0.167 (delta -0.001).
answers.does_combined_outperform_either_alone: On canonical activation PCA, combined R2 0.585 is not above the best single family (0.613). On Claude pseudo-PCA, combined R2 0.150 is not above the best single/full Claude family (0.243).
answers.are_codex_and_claude_complementary: Mixed but not strongly complementary in this benchmark. Big Five carries strong transferable signal into canonical activation geometry, while Codex retained features do not improve the direct Claude pseudo-PCA target over the semantic baseline; combined features should be read as complementary only where held-out R2 and residual reduction both improve.
answers.which_target_produces_stronger_agreement: Canonical activation PCA produces the cleaner cross-family comparison because neither feature family defines the target; Claude pseudo-PCA remains important but Big Five is close to a native positive-control target there.
answers.which_personas_consistently_well_explain: teacher, veteran, guardian, void, novelist, influencer, provincial, scheduler
answers.which_personas_consistently_poorly_expla: toddler, procrastinator, teenager, comedian, fool, infant, amateur, adolescent
answers.does_big_five_survive_direct_target_alig: Yes for canonical activation alignment: Big Five improves activation PCA by +0.224 R2 over semantic baseline.
answers.does_trait_plus_procedural_interpretatio: Supported as a bounded interpretation: trait-style and procedural/behavioral features both carry predictive signal, but neither should be treated as final or causal.
